cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Not the Real Fear
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation focused on practical details so no one reaches the fear underneath them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Before I open the scholarship letter, do we have clean teaspoons? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've made your tea. Open it; I want to know if you're leaving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. You've put sugar in mine. I'll need another cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Take mine. Are you frightened of going, or staying here with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If we swap cups, how will you know which has sugar? We need labels before anything gets mixed up.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 and A5 use tea logistics to evade fear, but A3 authority announcement offers no actual negotiated adjustment.

responseLogic.evidence: B4 cup swap can be tracked without labels; A5 excessive requirement is an avoidance tactic, not genuine physical necessity.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants the letter opened and B4 solves the cup issue while asking about leaving versus staying.

heightening.evidence: B4 solves the practical obstacle and names fear; A5 converts the solution into another practical delay.

specificity.evidence: A1 scholarship letter and B2 possible departure establish why the tea tasks are evasive.

brevityWit.evidence: A1 voluntary please and A3 status phrase detract from the otherwise concrete tea instructions.
